key_insight: Computer-vision-informed void nucleation makes a mesoscale damage model sensitive to microstructure and enables prediction of shock-induced spallation in tantalum.
engineering_relevance: The approach links grain-scale structure to plate-impact response, supporting microstructure-aware assessment of high-rate material failure.
method: Predict a void-nucleation susceptibility field from grain orientations and grain-boundary energy.
Gate nucleation by local maximum principal stress and model subsequent void growth.
Couple damage to crystal plasticity in a Lagrangian shock simulation with selectively resolved microstructure.
evidence_signal: Calibrated at 196 m/s flyer velocity, the model reproduced key experimental free-surface velocity features and transferred to 214 m/s without parameter changes.
watch_item: Accurate predictions depend on representative microstructures, and late-time free-surface velocity ringing showed deviations.
paper_title: A mesoscale damage model for void nucleation and growth in shock loaded microstructure informed by computer vision
